entry_state: The group extension binds calculations to books, branches and evidence views, preserves retries and leaves legal books intact. Eliminating an intragroup loan does not erase its currency exposure; settlement facts determine profit versus OCI. Transaction identity and control intervals govern eliminations. Hyperinflation restatement precedes translation, with monetary exposure, turnover and first-application tax handled separately. The exchangeability section has just introduced currency direction, date and purpose.
exit_state: Chapter 10 ends with purpose-specific exchangeability, the amended estimation objective and distinct initial-application adjustments. Financing, awards, EPS and consolidation all require contract rights, measurement origins, dates and reporting populations that closing totals cannot replace. The next chapter turns to credit losses and the bank balance sheet.
findings: The exchangeability method uses the inspected 2024 EU amendment for its effective periods, distinguishes ability from intention and does not invent an accessible-rate estimator.
Initial application separates retained-earnings and translation-reserve effects. The existing closed group profile is not silently extended. Chapter 10 is now fully read; no new confirmed defect.
